narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that, according to patterns seen across many similar employees, strongly signal higher turnover risk.

The most influential factor is your relatively short overall career experience. With only 1-5 years of total professional experience, you fall into the group where half of those predicted to stay also sit; however, the model sees this limited tenure as increasing the likelihood of moving on to new opportunities elsewhere. 

The second strongest influence is that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities is one of the clearest indicators the model uses for predicting departure, as it suggests viable alternatives are already available to you.

Third, the amount of time you have spent in your current role (also 1-5 years) further pushes the prediction toward leaving. Although this duration matches many employees who stay, when combined with your limited total experience and active job offers, it reinforces the impression that you are still early in your career and likely to explore other paths.

Taken together, these elements outweigh other factors such as your medical sector role, lack of recent training, or feelings of low recognition. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion timelines or development support, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current path truly aligns with your longer-term goals.
